posture: The shielded-pool TransferCircuit does not bind the spent note to the Merkle leaf, so any prover who sees one public tree path withdraws arbitrary amounts with fresh nullifiers; a Groth16 PoC shows two forged proofs verifying. Even with that fixed, the leaf index never drives the Merkle path, so one note yields unlimited nullifiers and right-side notes cannot be withdrawn. On the integration side, Pool calls verifyProof(bytes,uint256[7]) while the gnark-exported verifier exposes verifyProof(uint256[8],uint256[7]), so every withdrawal reverts today; this masks the circuit bugs until someone wires an adapter. SigCircuit accepts a forged EdDSA signature with R = (0,0) under gnark v0.14.0 and checks a raw emulated limb instead of the value; it has no consumer in the repository. Keys come from a single-party groth16.Setup that discards the proving key, and the committed Verifier.sol is a placeholder, so the trust in the deployed verifying key cannot be established from the code. The most important action is to recompute the note commitment in-circuit and derive both the nullifier and the path directions from it before any deployment.
out_of_scope: No Circom or Noir sources are present.
Solidity beyond the ZK integration surface (Pool.sol, Verifier.sol) was reviewed only through lenses I1-I3; no solidity-auditor companion was installed.
The off-chain Merkle tree builder, deposit flow and prover service are not in the repository.
gnark std gadgets were read at v0.14.0 only along the paths the circuits use (eddsa, twistededwards, emulated Mul, bits, MiMC).

records.title: Merkle leaf is never derived from the spent note, so anyone withdraws arbitrary amounts with fresh nullifiers
records.description: Any prover uses any public leaf path and a fresh Secret, because Path[0] is never computed from Secret, In.Value or In.Owner and the nullifier hashes only Secret and Index.
records.proof: Victim leaf L with siblings S1..S3 under root R (computed natively with gnark-crypto bn254 MiMC). Attacker witness: Path=[L,S1,S2,S3], Root=R, Secret=k for k=1 and k=2, Index=1, Nullifier=MiMC(k,1), In.Value=Out.Value=2^64-1, In.Owner=Out.Owner=0, Fees=(0,1), Recipient=0xdeadbeef, Extra=[0,0]. Both witnesses satisfy every constraint and both Groth16 proofs verify against the same root with distinct nullifiers.
records.impact: Any caller drains the Pool in withdrawals of up to 2^64-1 wei each, repeated without limit, without owning a deposit (once a verifier with the matching ABI is wired).

gates.executes: Every constraint on the path was traced (transfer.go:47-93); none links Path[0] to Secret or In. PoC solves and verifies.
gates.reachable: Leaf paths are public tree data; Secret, Index and In are free private witnesses.
gates.unprivileged: Any prover and any caller of Pool.withdraw.
gates.impact: Soundness: forged membership and unlimited nullifiers; Pool pays the public value.

fix.summary: Compute the note commitment in-circuit, use it as the Merkle leaf, and derive the nullifier from the same secret and leaf position.

options.label: Option A: bind the leaf to the note
options.diff:
-	cur := c.Path[0]
+	h.Reset()
+	h.Write(c.Secret, c.In.Value, c.In.Owner)
+	leaf := h.Sum()
+	api.AssertIsEqual(c.Path[0], leaf)
+	cur := leaf

options.label: Option B: derive the nullifier from the leaf
options.diff:
-	h.Write(c.Secret, c.Index)
+	h.Write(c.Secret, leaf, c.Index)  // after leaf is computed and Index drives the path bits

poc.command: GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=off timeout 600 go -C <out>/worktree-1 test -run PoC_ -count=1 -v ./circuit/
poc.output_excerpt: ATTACK: both forged groth16 proofs verify against the same root with different nullifiers; CONTROL: rejected as expected: constraint #2641 is not satisfied; SANITY: honest witness passes

refuter.reasoning: No constraint ties Path[0] to Secret, Index, In.Value or In.Owner (transfer.go:47-56); the remaining constraints (64, 70-72, 74-75, 77, 80, 83, 91) are satisfied with In=Out=V, q=1, Fees=(0,1). Pool.withdraw checks only knownRoots and a fresh nullifier (Pool.sol:39-40) and pays value (Pool.sol:51).

records.title: Index never drives the Merkle path, so one note yields unlimited nullifiers and right-side notes are unprovable
records.description: The nullifier hashes a prover-chosen Index that the path loop never reads, and the loop always hashes (cur, sibling), so Index is free and right-child leaves cannot be proven.
records.proof: Depth-3 tree of 8 leaves with node = MiMC(left, right). Note at leaf 0 with honest path: Index=1 and Index=2 with the same Path, Root and Secret both satisfy, give distinct nullifiers, and both Groth16 proofs verify. Index=2 with nullifier MiMC(s,1) is rejected (control). The honest leaf-1 witness (right child) fails at the root assertion, while leaf 0 passes.
records.impact: A note holder withdraws the same note repeatedly, which persists after the leaf-binding fix; holders of notes at right-child positions can never withdraw.

gates.executes: Index appears only at transfer.go:47 and :82; the loop at :51-55 has no direction selection. PoC verifies two proofs for one note.
gates.reachable: Index is a private witness; every note at a non-zero position hits the completeness break.
gates.unprivileged: Any note holder (and, with the leaf bug, anyone).
gates.impact: Soundness: double spend; completeness: funds of most depositors locked.

fix.summary: Decompose Index into Depth bits and use each bit to order (cur, sibling) at each level, so the nullifier's Index is the leaf's real position.

options.label: Option A: path direction bits from Index
options.diff:
+	idxBits := bits.ToBinary(api, c.Index, bits.WithNbDigits(Depth))
 	cur := c.Path[0]
 	for i := 1; i < len(c.Path); i++ {
 		h.Reset()
-		h.Write(cur, c.Path[i])
+		left := api.Select(idxBits[i-1], c.Path[i], cur)
+		right := api.Select(idxBits[i-1], cur, c.Path[i])
+		h.Write(left, right)
 		cur = h.Sum()
 	}

options.label: Option B: nullifier from the leaf only
options.diff:
-	h.Write(c.Secret, c.Index)
+	h.Write(c.Secret, leaf)  // leaf = note commitment; still add direction bits for completeness

poc.command: GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=off timeout 600 go -C <out>/worktree-2 test -run PoC_ -count=1 -v ./circuit/
poc.output_excerpt: ATTACK: two Groth16 proofs with distinct nullifiers verify for one note; CONTROL: mismatched nullifier rejected; COMPLETENESS: honest leaf 1 rejected

refuter.reasoning: Index enters only the nullifier hash (transfer.go:47-48) and IsZero (transfer.go:82); the Merkle loop (transfer.go:50-56) uses only Path and Root. Varying Index with a fixed witness gives fresh nullifiers accepted by Pool.sol:40,50. The fixed left-first order at transfer.go:53 cannot express right-child leaves.

records.title: EdDSA verification accepts R = (0,0), so any prover forges a signature for any key and message
records.description: Any prover sets Sig.R = (0,0), because gnark v0.14.0 eddsa.Verify never checks R is on the curve and the first cofactor Double divides 0 by 0, leaving its X output free.
records.proof: S=1, any PubKey A, any Msg: Q = [1]G - [h]A passes AssertIsOnCurve (eddsa.go:62). Add(Neg(Q), (0,0)) = (0,0) (point.go:34-59, denominators 1). Double #1 of (0,0): X = DivUnchecked(0,0) is constrained only by 0*X = 0 (r1cs api.go:258-261); set X = sqrt(-1) mod r, Y = 0. Double #2 of (i,0) = (0,-1); Double #3 = (0,1); eddsa.go:84-85 pass. A constraint model of the cofactor tail (first X division replaced by a hint with the identical R1C) produces a verifying Groth16 proof; the honest gnark solver leaves the 0/0 wire at 0, so the attack needs a prover with a modified solver, which constraints do not prevent.
records.impact: Any consumer that trusts a SigCircuit proof as signature authentication is fully bypassed; the repository has no such consumer today.

gates.executes: Each step traced against gnark v0.14.0 eddsa.go:41-87, point.go:34-81 and r1cs api.go:258-261; refuter re-derived it; model PoC verifies.
gates.reachable: Sig.R and S are secret witnesses chosen by the prover.
gates.impact: Soundness: forged signature for any public key and message.

fix.summary: Assert that Sig.R and PubKey.A are on the curve (and reject small-order points) before eddsa.Verify, and upgrade gnark.

options.label: Option A: explicit on-curve checks

poc.output_excerpt: attack: groth16 proof that off-curve Sig.R=(0,0) cofactor-clears to (0,1) VERIFIED (constraint model of the cofactor tail); control: honest solver rejects R=(0,0)

refuter.reasoning: eddsa.Verify (eddsa.go:41-87) checks only S <= Order (:57), Q on curve (:62) and Q == (0,1) (:84-85). With R=(0,0) the add yields (0,0); DivUnchecked (r1cs api.go:258-261) emits only d1*X == n1, which is 0*X == 0, so X is free; a = -1 (gnark-crypto bn254/twistededwards curve.go:44) makes X = sqrt(-1) reach (0,1) after two more doublings.

records.title: divHint quotient is checked in the field without its remainder
records.description: Any prover passes q = In.Value / Out.Value in the field, because only q*Out.Value == In.Value is asserted and the remainder is dropped; honest provers fail when Out.Value does not divide In.Value.
records.proof: In.Value=10, Out.Value=3, rest of the witness honest: the honest divHint (q=3) fails at constraint 1*9 != 10; with divHint overridden to q = 10*3^-1 mod r the system is solved. In.Value=9, Out.Value=3 passes with honest hints.
records.impact: Honest users cannot withdraw any amount that does not divide their note value, and the intended integer relation is never enforced.

gates.executes: transfer.go:62-64 is the only use of q; res[1] is discarded at :63. PoC solves with the override.
gates.reachable: Any Out.Value that does not divide In.Value (most partial withdrawals).
gates.impact: Completeness: honest withdrawals blocked; soundness: the divisibility rule is vacuous.

fix.summary: Constrain q*Out.Value + rem == In.Value with q and rem range-checked and rem < Out.Value, or remove the check if divisibility is not intended.

options.label: Option A: full Euclidean division
options.diff:
-	_ = res[1]
-	api.AssertIsEqual(api.Mul(q, c.Out.Value), c.In.Value)
+	rem := res[1]
+	bits.ToBinary(api, q, bits.WithNbDigits(64))
+	bits.ToBinary(api, rem, bits.WithNbDigits(64))
+	api.AssertIsEqual(api.Add(api.Mul(q, c.Out.Value), rem), c.In.Value)
+	api.AssertIsLessOrEqual(api.Add(rem, 1), c.Out.Value)

options.label: Option B: drop the division
options.diff:
-	res, err := api.Compiler().NewHint(divHint, 2, c.In.Value, c.Out.Value)
-	...
-	api.AssertIsEqual(api.Mul(q, c.Out.Value), c.In.Value)

records.title: Nonzero check reads one limb of an unreduced emulated product
records.description: Any prover passes Amount = n (zero mod n) with a Mul remainder of n, because the remainder is only width-checked and sig.go:39 tests a raw limb instead of the value.
records.proof: Amount limbs = n (secp256k1 order); emulated mulHint overridden to return remainder = n, quotient = n-1 with recomputed carries; sq.Limbs[0] = 0xbfd25e8cd0364141 and a Groth16 proof verifies. The honest hint rejects Amount = n; honest Amount = 2^32 is rejected (completeness); Amount = 3 passes.
records.impact: The intended Amount^2 != 0 rule accepts a zero amount and rejects some valid amounts; no consumer of SigCircuit exists in the repository.

gates.executes: Remainder packed with packLimbs(..., true) (gnark v0.14.0 field_mul.go:507), width-only; no ReduceStrict or AssertIsInRange on the path. PoC verifies.
gates.reachable: Amount is a secret emulated witness accepted below 2^256.
gates.impact: Soundness of the nonzero rule and completeness for amounts whose square has a zero low limb.

fix.summary: Test the value, not a limb: assert f.IsZero(sq) == 0, or reduce strictly before reading limbs.

poc.command: GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=off timeout 600 go -C <out>/worktree-5 test -run PoC_ -count=1 -v ./circuit/
poc.output_excerpt: attack accepted: Amount = n (== 0 mod n), sq.Limbs[0] = 0xbfd25e8cd0364141; attack: Groth16 proof with Amount = n verifies; honest Amount = 2^32 rejected (completeness bug)

refuter.reasoning: The Amount witness is only limb-width checked (field.go:245, field_assert.go:23-29); the Mul remainder is packed width-only (field_mul.go:507) with no strict < p check in mulMod (field_mul.go:229-252); quotient n-1 fits the quotient limbs; the deferred polynomial identity holds since n*n = n + (n-1)*n.

records.title: Pool calls a verifyProof signature that the gnark-exported verifier does not have
records.description: Every withdrawal reverts, because Pool calls verifyProof(bytes,uint256[7]) while gnark v0.14.0 ExportSolidity emits only verifyProof(uint256[8],uint256[7]) and no fallback.
records.proof: Foundry test with the real verifier exported by vk.ExportSolidity for TransferCircuit (Extra length 2) and a real Groth16 proof: calling the verifier directly with uint256[8] succeeds, a tampered input reverts, Pool.withdraw with the same proof reverts with empty revert data and leaves the nullifier unspent, and the same withdraw through a bytes-to-uint256[8] adapter succeeds.
records.impact: No user can withdraw until the owner deploys an adapter or a different verifier through setVerifier.

gates.executes: Selectors differ; generated template has no fallback (gnark v0.14.0 backend/groth16/bn254/solidity.go:680-687). Foundry PoC passes 5/5.
gates.reachable: Every withdraw against the verifier that cmd/setup exports.
gates.unprivileged: Hits every honest user; recovery needs the owner.
gates.impact: Completeness: the core withdraw flow is bricked (recoverable by the owner).

fix.summary: Match the generated ABI in IVerifier and pass the proof as uint256[8].

options.label: Option A: fix the interface
options.diff:
-    function verifyProof(bytes calldata proof, uint256[7] calldata input) external view;
+    function verifyProof(uint256[8] calldata proof, uint256[7] calldata input) external view;

poc.command: go -C <out>/worktree-7 test -run PoC_7_Gen ./circuit/ && forge test --root <out>/worktree-7 --match-contract PoC_7 -vv --offline

(solidity.go:520) and verifyProof(uint256[8],...) (solidity.go:680-687); the only options (backend/solidity/solidity.go:38,49) do not change the signature; no fallback exists.

records.title: gnark v0.14.0 is affected by three std soundness advisories
records.description: go.mod pins gnark v0.14.0, affected by GHSA-3mvx-pp85-pm65 (std emulated arithmetic and others, fixed v0.16.2), GHSA-7fx8-hmgc-82jp (fake-GLV / ECDSA, fixed v0.16.4) and GHSA-fwf3-jmp7-gmrj (pairing G2 check, fixed v0.16.0); SigCircuit uses emulated arithmetic (circuit/sig.go:34-38).

records.impact: Emulated-arithmetic soundness bugs in the pinned std version can affect SigCircuit; SigCircuit has no consumer in the repository.

gates.executes: Advisory table match on go.mod:8; affected component imported at circuit/sig.go:8.
gates.impact: Soundness of emulated arithmetic in SigCircuit; capped at medium because nothing consumes SigCircuit.

records.title: change <= In.Value comparison on a wrapped Sub
records.description: Inventory flagged AssertIsLessOrEqual(change, In.Value) with change = In - Out as a wrapped comparison.
records.reason: In.Value < 2^64 is enforced by the 32-bit limb recomposition, and AssertIsLessOrEqual decomposes the bound canonically; a wrapped change r - d (or its alias + r) exceeds In.Value, so the check enforces Out.Value <= In.Value.

records.title: Recipient can be swapped on a submitted proof
records.description: V-pubin claimed Recipient is not pinned because its only use is a discarded IsZero.
records.reason: IsZero emits R1CS rows over Recipient, so its Groth16 IC point is non-zero and a third party cannot change recipient on an existing proof; choosing the recipient when proving is the witness holder's intended right (I1, G2, F1, C6 agree).

records.title: Go nil check on Index skips constraints
records.description: Inventory flagged `if c.Index == nil` as Go control flow on a witness.
records.reason: At compile time Index holds a schema placeholder, never nil, so the Extra booleanity constraints are always emitted; the branch never fires for the compiled system.

records.title: verifyProof result is not checked

records.reason: The Groth16 verifier signature returns nothing and reverts on failure; a void external call to an address without code also reverts, so no unchecked boolean exists.
